blocks.text: King George Corridor, South Surrey: Neighbourhood Guide
Living along the King George Corridor

parts.t: King George Corridor is the MLS® sub-area along King George Boulevard in South Surrey. The City’s plan area runs about 7 km from 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River, with Highway 99 on the east side. The road follows part of the Semiahmoo Trail, a route in use by 1858, and royal oaks planted for the 1937 coronation still line it. Bus rapid transit is now being designed for the boulevard, so it pays to look up plans for the blocks near a home.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Planning on the King George Corridor

parts.t: The 1995 corridor plan now guides parks and services, while the OCP sets land use.
The King George Corridor plan was completed in 1995. On December 2, 2024, Council endorsed Corporate Report R246 to update its land use designations.
Its land use designations are now superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP, but the plan still guides public amenities and infrastructure.
King George Boulevard bus rapid transit moved to full design in May 2026.
The royal oaks and the Semiahmoo Trail are City heritage sites, which can affect work near them.

blocks.text: King George Corridor questions

parts.t: Where is the King George Corridor?

Along King George Boulevard in South Surrey, from 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River, with Highway 99 to the east. The MLS® sub-area lines are set by the real estate board, so check where a listing is placed.
How big is the King George Corridor plan area?
About 490 hectares (1,210 acres) over roughly 7 km. The plan’s land use designations are now superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP, but it still guides public amenities and infrastructure. See the
Is bus rapid transit coming to King George Boulevard?

It is being designed. The line is planned with 12 stations over 19 km from Surrey City Centre to Semiahmoo Town Centre, and Council approved full design in May 2026. TransLink notes the project is not yet funded, so timing is not set.
The first widening contracts, approved in May 2026, are for a third southbound lane between 72 and 76 Avenue, well north of South Surrey.
